manifest.title: Temporal graphs, temporal settings, traversal times, reachability, and optimal temporal paths

inputs.abstract:
[Read the annotated paper](paper.html) for a short introduction with the formal definitions, results, and proofs alongside the text.

We give three representations of finite temporal graphs on a fixed vertex set: (1) a sequence of snapshots, (2) a footprint with finite time labels, and (3) a chronological list of temporal edge occurrences. Equal-time edge occurrences have no prescribed order.

We define strict and nonstrict temporal walks, paths, reachability and temporal graph settings. Removing a closed segment turns a walk into a shorter walk with the same endpoints. On proper graphs, the departure times of every nonstrict path are already strictly increasing. Examples distinguish paths from walks, simplicity from properness, and illustrate why opposite arcs may share a timestamp.

An occurrence may have a natural traversal time. Waiting is allowed, the lifetime bounds departure times, and the final arrival may follow the last snapshot. Uniform traversal times one and zero recover strict and nonstrict paths respectively, with the same vertices and departure times, and therefore the same reachability.

We define five interpretations of optimal temporal paths for a fixed source, target, release time and arrival deadline: shortest, fastest, foremost, latest-departure and minimum-waiting paths. Each objective admits an optimal path whenever the query is feasible. With uniform traversal time c, elapsed time is total internal waiting plus c times the number of hops. Three-vertex examples separate all five optimality predicates for strict temporal paths (uniform traversal time one). For nonstrict paths (uniform traversal time zero), fastest and minimum waiting coincide.
## Guide to the concepts

- [Three representations of temporal graphs](Lax330177.Representations.html) defines snapshots, time-labelled footprints and chronological event lists, and proves how to convert between them.
- [Temporal graph settings](Lax330177.Settings.html) defines directed and undirected settings, strict and nonstrict modes, and simple, proper and happy labellings.
- [Paths, walks and reachability](Lax330177.Paths.html) defines timed walks, paths and reachability. It proves that deleting cycles preserves reachability and that strict and nonstrict paths coincide on proper graphs.
- [Traversal times](Lax330177.Durations.html) allows each edge occurrence its own traversal time and proves that uniform times zero and one recover nonstrict and strict paths, respectively.
- [Counterexamples](Lax330177.Examples.html) separates simplicity from properness, shows why the proper-path theorem fails for walks, and gives a happy undirected graph with asymmetric, nontransitive reachability.
- [Optimal temporal paths](Lax330177.OptimalPaths.html) defines shortest, fastest, foremost, latest-departure and minimum-waiting paths and proves that each optimum is attained whenever a feasible path exists.
- [Optimality under uniform traversal times](Lax330177.UniformCosts.html) expresses elapsed time in terms of hops and waiting and proves what fastest paths minimize at traversal times zero and one.
- [Three-vertex examples separating path objectives](Lax330177.CostExamples.html) compares routes on a chain and on a triangle to show which optimality criteria can select different paths.
- [The temporal reachability graph](Lax330177.ReachabilityGraph.html) records reachable pairs of distinct vertices as arcs of a static digraph.

concepts.title: Three-vertex examples separating path objectives
concepts.description:
The chain 0 → 1 → 2 is available at times 0 through 3. An optional shortcut
0 → 2 makes a triangle. Every traversal takes c units, where c is zero or one.
In the triangle compare the direct departures at 0 and 3 with the two-hop
journey departing at 0 and c. In the chain compare departures (0,3) with (0,c).
These witnesses distinguish optimality predicates, allowing ties.

- [Early and late direct paths.](Lax330177Proofs.CostExamples.direct_choices.html) In the triangle, direct departures at 0 and 3 both minimize hops, elapsed time and waiting for either traversal cost. Of these two paths, only the early one is foremost and only the late one is latest-departing.
- [A shortest path can wait longer.](Lax330177Proofs.CostExamples.slow_shortest.html) On the chain without the shortcut, departures at 0 and 3 give a shortest path for either traversal cost. Another feasible path arrives in less elapsed time and has less total waiting.
- [A detour with no waiting.](Lax330177Proofs.CostExamples.no_wait_detour.html) In the triangle, the two-hop path departing at 0 and c minimizes waiting for either traversal cost and uses more hops than the shortcut. It is fastest exactly when c is zero.

/-!
---
title: Three-vertex examples separating path objectives
type: definition
---
The chain 0 → 1 → 2 is available at times 0 through 3. An optional shortcut
0 → 2 makes a triangle. Every traversal takes c units, where c is zero or one.
In the triangle compare the direct departures at 0 and 3 with the two-hop
journey departing at 0 and c. In the chain compare departures (0,3) with (0,c).
These witnesses distinguish optimality predicates, allowing ties.

- [Early and late direct paths.](Lax330177Proofs.CostExamples.direct_choices.html) In the triangle, direct departures at 0 and 3 both minimize hops, elapsed time and waiting for either traversal cost. Of these two paths, only the early one is foremost and only the late one is latest-departing.
- [A shortest path can wait longer.](Lax330177Proofs.CostExamples.slow_shortest.html) On the chain without the shortcut, departures at 0 and 3 give a shortest path for either traversal cost. Another feasible path arrives in less elapsed time and has less total waiting.
- [A detour with no waiting.](Lax330177Proofs.CostExamples.no_wait_detour.html) In the triangle, the two-hop path departing at 0 and c minimizes waiting for either traversal cost and uses more hops than the shortcut. It is fastest exactly when c is zero.
-/
namespace Lax330177.CostExamples
open Lax330177.Representations Lax330177.Durations Lax330177.OptimalPaths

abbrev network (shortcut : Bool) : Graph 3 where
  lifetime := 4
  edge _ u v := u.val + 1 = v.val ∨ (shortcut = true ∧ u = 0 ∧ v = 2)
  loopless := by intro t u; fin_cases u <;> simp

def query (shortcut : Bool) (c : Fin 2) : Query (network shortcut) where
  source := 0
  target := 2
  release := 0
  deadline := 3+c.val
  transit _ _ _ := c.val

def direct (late : Bool) (c : Fin 2) : Candidate (query true c) where
  hops := 1
  vertex := ![0,2]
  time := fun _ => if late then 3 else 0
  departure := if late then 3 else 0
  arrival := (if late then 3 else 0) + c.val
  feasible := by cases late <;> fin_cases c <;> dsimp [DurationPath, Feasible, query, network] <;> decide
  starts := rfl
  ends := rfl
  released := by cases late <;> fin_cases c <;> dsimp [DurationPath, Feasible, query, network] <;> decide
  inOrder := by cases late <;> fin_cases c <;> dsimp [DurationPath, Feasible, query, network] <;> decide
  onTime := by cases late <;> fin_cases c <;> dsimp [DurationPath, Feasible, query, network] <;> decide
  first := by cases late <;> fin_cases c <;> dsimp [DurationPath, Feasible, query, network] <;> decide
  last := by cases late <;> fin_cases c <;> dsimp [DurationPath, Feasible, query, network] <;> decide
  instantaneous := by cases late <;> fin_cases c <;> dsimp [DurationPath, Feasible, query, network] <;> decide

def via (shortcut slow : Bool) (c : Fin 2) : Candidate (query shortcut c) where
  hops := 2
  vertex := id
  time := ![0, if slow then 3 else ⟨c.val, by change c.val < 4; omega⟩]
  departure := 0
  arrival := (if slow then 3 else c.val) + c.val
  feasible := by cases shortcut <;> cases slow <;> fin_cases c <;> dsimp [DurationPath, Feasible, query, network] <;> decide
  starts := rfl
  ends := rfl
  released := by cases shortcut <;> cases slow <;> fin_cases c <;> dsimp [DurationPath, Feasible, query, network] <;> decide
  inOrder := by cases shortcut <;> cases slow <;> fin_cases c <;> dsimp [DurationPath, Feasible, query, network] <;> decide
  onTime := by cases shortcut <;> cases slow <;> fin_cases c <;> dsimp [DurationPath, Feasible, query, network] <;> decide
  first := by cases shortcut <;> cases slow <;> fin_cases c <;> dsimp [DurationPath, Feasible, query, network] <;> decide
  last := by cases shortcut <;> cases slow <;> fin_cases c <;> dsimp [DurationPath, Feasible, query, network] <;> decide
  instantaneous := by cases shortcut <;> cases slow <;> fin_cases c <;> dsimp [DurationPath, Feasible, query, network] <;> decide



end Lax330177.CostExamples

concepts.title: Traversal times
concepts.description:
Each occurrence has a natural traversal time. The next departure may occur at arrival. The lifetime bounds departure times and the final arrival may fall outside it.

- [Feasible departure times.](Lax330177Proofs.Basic.uniform_modes.html) For integer timestamps, a departure sequence is feasible with traversal time zero exactly when it is weakly increasing. With traversal time one, it is feasible exactly when it is strictly increasing.
- [The same timed paths.](Lax330177Proofs.Basic.uniform_paths.html) Fix the vertex sequence and every departure time. They form a path with uniform traversal time zero exactly when they form a nonstrict temporal path, and with uniform time one exactly when they form a strict temporal path.
- [The same reachable pairs.](Lax330177Proofs.Basic.uniform_reaches.html) For every pair of vertices, reachability with uniform traversal time zero is equivalent to nonstrict reachability, and reachability with uniform time one is equivalent to strict reachability.

import Mathlib
import Lax330177.Representations
import Lax330177.Paths

/-!
---
title: Traversal times
type: definition
---
Each occurrence has a natural traversal time. The next departure may occur at arrival. The lifetime bounds departure times and the final arrival may fall outside it.

- [Feasible departure times.](Lax330177Proofs.Basic.uniform_modes.html) For integer timestamps, a departure sequence is feasible with traversal time zero exactly when it is weakly increasing. With traversal time one, it is feasible exactly when it is strictly increasing.
- [The same timed paths.](Lax330177Proofs.Basic.uniform_paths.html) Fix the vertex sequence and every departure time. They form a path with uniform traversal time zero exactly when they form a nonstrict temporal path, and with uniform time one exactly when they form a strict temporal path.
- [The same reachable pairs.](Lax330177Proofs.Basic.uniform_reaches.html) For every pair of vertices, reachability with uniform traversal time zero is equivalent to nonstrict reachability, and reachability with uniform time one is equivalent to strict reachability.
-/
namespace Lax330177.Durations
open Lax330177.Representations
open Lax330177.Paths
noncomputable section
attribute [local instance] Classical.propDecidable

def Feasible {k : ℕ} (time duration : Fin k → ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∀ i j, i < j → time i + duration i ≤ time j

def DurationPath {n k} (G : Graph n) (δ : Fin G.lifetime → Fin n → Fin n → ℕ)
    (x : Fin (k+1) → Fin n) (t : Fin k → Fin G.lifetime) : Prop :=
  Function.Injective x ∧ (∀ i, G.edge (t i) (x i.castSucc) (x i.succ)) ∧
    Feasible (fun i => (t i).val) (fun i => δ (t i) (x i.castSucc) (x i.succ))


def DurationReaches {n} (G : Graph n) (δ : Fin G.lifetime → Fin n → Fin n → ℕ)
    (u v : Fin n) : Prop :=
  ∃ k, ∃ x : Fin (k+1) → Fin n, ∃ t : Fin k → Fin G.lifetime,
    DurationPath G δ x t ∧ x 0 = u ∧ x (Fin.last k) = v



end
end Lax330177.Durations

concepts.title: Counterexamples
concepts.description:
A single repeated edge admits a simultaneous return walk under properness. A chain in reverse chronological order witnesses failure of transitivity.

- [A simple graph can separate the traversal modes.](Lax330177Proofs.Basic.simple_separation.html) The directed chain with both arcs available only at time 0 is simple and fails properness. Its first vertex reaches its last nonstrictly but cannot reach it strictly.
- [Properness does not imply simplicity.](Lax330177Proofs.Basic.proper_separation.html) One undirected edge appearing twice gives a proper graph that fails simplicity. The two opposite directed arcs are proper as well, since every two-step traversal returns to its starting vertex.
- [A proper graph can have a walk with equal departure times.](Lax330177Proofs.Basic.bounce_same_time.html) On a proper undirected graph, a nonstrict walk can traverse one edge and immediately traverse it back at the same time.
- [Reachability can fail transitivity.](Lax330177Proofs.Basic.chain_failure.html) In both traversal modes, the same three-vertex chain has 0 reaching 1 and 1 reaching 2, although 0 cannot reach 2.
- [Reachability can be asymmetric even on a happy graph.](Lax330177Proofs.Basic.happy_asymmetry.html) The undirected chain with edge 1–2 at time 0 and edge 0–1 at time 1 is simple and proper. In both modes, 2 reaches 0 while 0 cannot reach 2.
- [A temporal-edge trail can repeat a static edge.](Lax330177.TrailSeparation.html) Crossing one undirected edge at time 0 and returning at time 1 gives a temporal-edge trail that repeats its static edge.

namespace Lax330177.Examples
open Lax330177.Representations
open Lax330177.Settings
open Lax330177.Paths
noncomputable section
attribute [local instance] Classical.propDecidable
abbrev repeatedEdge : Graph 2 where
  lifetime := 2
  edge _ u v := u ≠ v
  loopless := by intro _ _ h; exact h rfl

def bounce : Walk repeatedEdge .strict 2 where
  vertex := ![0, 1, 0]
  time := id
  available := by intro i; fin_cases i <;> decide
  ordered := by intro i j h; exact h




def simultaneousBounce : Walk repeatedEdge .nonstrict 2 where
  vertex := ![0, 1, 0]
  time _ := (0 : Fin 2)
  available := by intro i; fin_cases i <;> decide
  ordered := by intro i j _; exact le_refl _


abbrev backwardsChain : Graph 3 where
  lifetime := 2
  edge t u v :=
    (t = 1 ∧ ((u = 0 ∧ v = 1) ∨ (u = 1 ∧ v = 0))) ∨
    (t = 0 ∧ ((u = 1 ∧ v = 2) ∨ (u = 2 ∧ v = 1)))
  loopless := by intro t u; fin_cases t <;> fin_cases u <;> decide

def firstLeg : Walk backwardsChain .strict 1 where
  vertex := ![0, 1]
  time _ := (1 : Fin 2)
  available := by intro i; fin_cases i; decide
  ordered := by intro i j h; have := i.isLt; have := j.isLt; change i.val < j.val at h; omega

def secondLeg : Walk backwardsChain .strict 1 where
  vertex := ![1, 2]
  time _ := (0 : Fin 2)
  available := by intro i; fin_cases i; decide
  ordered := by intro i j h; have := i.isLt; have := j.isLt; change i.val < j.val at h; omega







abbrev simultaneousChain : Graph 3 where
  lifetime := 1
  edge _ u v := (u = 0 ∧ v = 1) ∨ (u = 1 ∧ v = 2)
  loopless := by intro t u; fin_cases u <;> decide

def chainPath : Walk simultaneousChain .nonstrict 2 where
  vertex := id
  time _ := 0
  available := by intro i; fin_cases i <;> decide
  ordered := by intro i j h; exact le_rfl



def reverseChainPath : Walk backwardsChain .strict 2 where
  vertex := ![2,1,0]
  time := id
  available := by intro i; fin_cases i <;> decide
  ordered := by intro i j h; exact h


end
end Lax330177.Examples

concepts.title: Labels to snapshots and back

concepts.title: Optimal temporal paths
concepts.description:
Fix two vertices, traversal times, a release time and an inclusive arrival deadline.
A shortest path minimizes traversals. A fastest path minimizes elapsed time from
first departure to final arrival. Foremost paths minimize arrival, and latest
departure paths maximize departure. Minimum waiting paths minimize the sum of
idle gaps at internal vertices. Initial waiting and time after arrival do not
contribute. A zero-edge path occupies its vertex at any one instant in the window.
Every feasible query admits an optimizer for each of the five criteria.

- [Each objective attains its optimum.](Lax330177Proofs.OptimalPaths.optima_exist.html) Fix the endpoints, traversal times, release time and arrival deadline. If at least one feasible path exists, then each of the five criteria has an optimal path. The optimizing path may depend on the criterion.

import Lax330177.Durations
import Mathlib.Order.Filter.Extr
import Mathlib.Algebra.BigOperators.Group.Finset.Basic

/-!
---
title: Optimal temporal paths
type: definition
---
Fix two vertices, traversal times, a release time and an inclusive arrival deadline.
A shortest path minimizes traversals. A fastest path minimizes elapsed time from
first departure to final arrival. Foremost paths minimize arrival, and latest
departure paths maximize departure. Minimum waiting paths minimize the sum of
idle gaps at internal vertices. Initial waiting and time after arrival do not
contribute. A zero-edge path occupies its vertex at any one instant in the window.
Every feasible query admits an optimizer for each of the five criteria.

- [Each objective attains its optimum.](Lax330177Proofs.OptimalPaths.optima_exist.html) Fix the endpoints, traversal times, release time and arrival deadline. If at least one feasible path exists, then each of the five criteria has an optimal path. The optimizing path may depend on the criterion.
-/
namespace Lax330177.OptimalPaths
open Lax330177.Representations Lax330177.Durations

structure Query {n : ℕ} (G : Graph n) where
  source : Fin n
  target : Fin n
  release : ℕ
  deadline : ℕ
  transit : Fin G.lifetime → Fin n → Fin n → ℕ

variable {n : ℕ} {G : Graph n} (q : Query G)

structure Candidate where
  hops : ℕ
  vertex : Fin (hops+1) → Fin n
  time : Fin hops → Fin G.lifetime
  feasible : DurationPath G q.transit vertex time
  starts : vertex 0 = q.source
  ends : vertex (Fin.last hops) = q.target
  departure : ℕ
  arrival : ℕ
  released : q.release ≤ departure
  inOrder : departure ≤ arrival
  onTime : arrival ≤ q.deadline
  first : ∀ h : 0 < hops, departure = (time ⟨0,h⟩).val
  last : ∀ h : 0 < hops,
    let i : Fin hops := ⟨hops-1, by omega⟩
    arrival = (time i).val + q.transit (time i) (vertex i.castSucc) (vertex i.succ)
  instantaneous : hops = 0 → departure = arrival

variable {q}
def Candidate.elapsed (p : Candidate q) := p.arrival - p.departure

def Candidate.waiting (p : Candidate q) : ℕ :=
  ∑ i : Fin p.hops, if h : i.val + 1 < p.hops then
    (p.time ⟨i.val+1,h⟩).val - ((p.time i).val + q.transit (p.time i) (p.vertex i.castSucc) (p.vertex i.succ))
  else 0

def Shortest (p : Candidate q) := IsMinOn Candidate.hops Set.univ p
def Fastest (p : Candidate q) := IsMinOn Candidate.elapsed Set.univ p
def Foremost (p : Candidate q) := IsMinOn Candidate.arrival Set.univ p
abbrev EarliestArrival (p : Candidate q) := Foremost p
def LatestDeparture (p : Candidate q) := IsMaxOn Candidate.departure Set.univ p
def MinimumWaiting (p : Candidate q) := IsMinOn Candidate.waiting Set.univ p

end Lax330177.OptimalPaths

concepts.title: Paths, walks and reachability
concepts.description:
Walks may revisit vertices. Paths have injective vertex sequences. Departure times increase strictly or weakly according to the traversal mode.

- [Walks and paths have the same reachability.](Lax330177Proofs.Basic.walk_path_reach.html) In either traversal mode, a temporal walk from u to v exists exactly when a temporal path from u to v exists.
- [Strict paths give nonstrict reachability.](Lax330177Proofs.Basic.strict_inclusion.html) If u can reach v by a strict temporal path, then u can also reach v by a nonstrict temporal path in the same graph.
- [Departure times on a proper graph.](Lax330177Proofs.Basic.proper_path_times.html) On a proper directed or undirected graph, every nonstrict temporal path already has strictly increasing departure times.
- [Reachability on a proper graph.](Lax330177Proofs.Basic.proper_modes.html) On a proper directed or undirected graph, u reaches v strictly exactly when u reaches v nonstrictly.
- [Replacing undirected edges by opposite arcs.](Lax330177Proofs.Basic.bidirect_paths.html) Replacing each undirected edge occurrence by both directed orientations preserves exactly the same timed paths of every length in the chosen traversal mode.
- [Path supports determine reachability.](Lax330177Proofs.Basic.support_reach.html) If two graphs on the same vertices realize exactly the same ordered vertex sequences as temporal paths in their respective modes, then they have the same reachability relation.
- [Temporal reachability is reflexive.](Lax330177.Reflexivity.html) Every vertex reaches itself in both modes, including at lifetime zero.
- [Enlarging the allowed vertex set.](Lax330177.RestrictedMonotonicity.html) A path restricted to C remains feasible in any vertex superset D.
- [Allowing all vertices.](Lax330177.UnrestrictedVertices.html) Restricting the path to the full vertex set recovers ordinary temporal reachability.
- [Paths are static-edge trails.](Lax330177.PathTrail.html) A vertex-simple path never uses a footprint edge twice, even counting reverse traversals as the same undirected edge.
- [Static-edge trails are temporal-edge trails.](Lax330177.TrailInclusion.html) A walk that never repeats a static edge never repeats an edge-time occurrence.
- [Strict walks are temporal-edge trails.](Lax330177.StrictWalkTrail.html) A strict walk never repeats an edge-time occurrence.
- [Properness of symmetric snapshots.](Lax330177.SymmetricProper.html) On symmetric snapshots, directed properness is equivalent to undirected properness.

import Lax330177.Representations
import Lax330177.Settings

/-!
---
title: Paths, walks and reachability
type: definition
---
Walks may revisit vertices. Paths have injective vertex sequences. Departure times increase strictly or weakly according to the traversal mode.

- [Walks and paths have the same reachability.](Lax330177Proofs.Basic.walk_path_reach.html) In either traversal mode, a temporal walk from u to v exists exactly when a temporal path from u to v exists.
- [Strict paths give nonstrict reachability.](Lax330177Proofs.Basic.strict_inclusion.html) If u can reach v by a strict temporal path, then u can also reach v by a nonstrict temporal path in the same graph.
- [Departure times on a proper graph.](Lax330177Proofs.Basic.proper_path_times.html) On a proper directed or undirected graph, every nonstrict temporal path already has strictly increasing departure times.
- [Reachability on a proper graph.](Lax330177Proofs.Basic.proper_modes.html) On a proper directed or undirected graph, u reaches v strictly exactly when u reaches v nonstrictly.
- [Replacing undirected edges by opposite arcs.](Lax330177Proofs.Basic.bidirect_paths.html) Replacing each undirected edge occurrence by both directed orientations preserves exactly the same timed paths of every length in the chosen traversal mode.
- [Path supports determine reachability.](Lax330177Proofs.Basic.support_reach.html) If two graphs on the same vertices realize exactly the same ordered vertex sequences as temporal paths in their respective modes, then they have the same reachability relation.
- [Temporal reachability is reflexive.](Lax330177.Reflexivity.html) Every vertex reaches itself in both modes, including at lifetime zero.
- [Enlarging the allowed vertex set.](Lax330177.RestrictedMonotonicity.html) A path restricted to C remains feasible in any vertex superset D.
- [Allowing all vertices.](Lax330177.UnrestrictedVertices.html) Restricting the path to the full vertex set recovers ordinary temporal reachability.
- [Paths are static-edge trails.](Lax330177.PathTrail.html) A vertex-simple path never uses a footprint edge twice, even counting reverse traversals as the same undirected edge.
- [Static-edge trails are temporal-edge trails.](Lax330177.TrailInclusion.html) A walk that never repeats a static edge never repeats an edge-time occurrence.
- [Strict walks are temporal-edge trails.](Lax330177.StrictWalkTrail.html) A strict walk never repeats an edge-time occurrence.
- [Properness of symmetric snapshots.](Lax330177.SymmetricProper.html) On symmetric snapshots, directed properness is equivalent to undirected properness.
-/
namespace Lax330177.Paths
open Lax330177.Representations
open Lax330177.Settings
noncomputable section
attribute [local instance] Classical.propDecidable
structure Walk {n : ℕ} (G : Graph n) (mode : TraversalMode) (k : ℕ) where
  vertex : Fin (k + 1) → Fin n
  time : Fin k → Fin G.lifetime
  available : ∀ i, G.edge (time i) (vertex i.castSucc) (vertex i.succ)
  ordered : ∀ i j, i < j → TimeLE mode (time i).val (time j).val

namespace Walk
variable {n k : ℕ} {G : Graph n} {mode : TraversalMode}

def start (w : Walk G mode k) := w.vertex 0
def finish (w : Walk G mode k) := w.vertex (Fin.last k)
def support (w : Walk G mode k) := List.ofFn w.vertex
def IsPath (w : Walk G mode k) : Prop := Function.Injective w.vertex
def IsStaticEdgeTrail (d : Direction) (w : Walk G mode k) : Prop :=
  ∀ i j : Fin k, SameStaticEdge d (w.vertex i.castSucc) (w.vertex i.succ)
    (w.vertex j.castSucc) (w.vertex j.succ) → i = j
def IsTemporalEdgeTrail (d : Direction) (w : Walk G mode k) : Prop :=
  ∀ i j : Fin k, SameStaticEdge d (w.vertex i.castSucc) (w.vertex i.succ)
    (w.vertex j.castSucc) (w.vertex j.succ) → w.time i = w.time j → i = j

def StaysIn (w : Walk G mode k) (C : Finset (Fin n)) : Prop := ∀ i, w.vertex i ∈ C
def InWindow (w : Walk G mode k) (a b : ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∀ i, a ≤ (w.time i).val ∧ (w.time i).val < b
def IsClosed (w : Walk G mode k) : Prop := w.start = w.finish
def IsCircuit (d : Direction) (w : Walk G mode k) : Prop :=
  0 < k ∧ w.IsClosed ∧ w.IsStaticEdgeTrail d
/-- Positive closed walk without repeated vertices except the final return.
Undirected cycles also have at least three edges, directed cycles at least two. -/
def IsCycle (d : Direction) (w : Walk G mode k) : Prop :=
  (match d with | .directed => 2 ≤ k | .undirected => 3 ≤ k) ∧
    w.IsClosed ∧ Function.Injective (fun i : Fin k => w.vertex i.castSucc)

def nil (G : Graph n) (mode : TraversalMode) (v : Fin n) : Walk G mode 0 where
  vertex _ := v
  time := Fin.elim0
  available := by intro i; exact Fin.elim0 i
  ordered := by intro i; exact Fin.elim0 i


def forgetStrict (w : Walk G .strict k) : Walk G .nonstrict k where
  vertex := w.vertex
  time := w.time
  available := w.available
  ordered := by intro i j h; exact Nat.le_of_lt (w.ordered i j h)







/-- A contiguous segment, including its two endpoints. -/
def segment (w : Walk G mode k) (a len : ℕ) (h : a + len ≤ k) :
    Walk G mode len where
  vertex i := w.vertex ⟨a + i.val, by omega⟩
  time i := w.time ⟨a + i.val, by omega⟩
  available i := w.available ⟨a + i.val, by omega⟩
  ordered := by intro i j hij; apply w.ordered; change a + i.val < a + j.val; omega

def take (w : Walk G mode k) (len : ℕ) (h : len ≤ k) := w.segment 0 len (by omega)
def suffix (w : Walk G mode k) (a : ℕ) (h : a ≤ k) :=
  w.segment a (k - a) (by omega)

/-- Boundary condition for concatenation; empty operands impose no time constraint. -/
def CanAppend {l : ℕ} (w : Walk G mode k) (z : Walk G mode l) : Prop :=
  w.finish = z.start ∧ ∀ i j, TimeLE mode (w.time i).val (z.time j).val

end Walk

def Reaches {n : ℕ} (G : Graph n) (mode : TraversalMode) (u v : Fin n) : Prop :=
  ∃ k, ∃ w : Walk G mode k, w.IsPath ∧ w.start = u ∧ w.finish = v
def WalkReaches {n : ℕ} (G : Graph n) (mode : TraversalMode) (u v : Fin n) : Prop :=
  ∃ k, ∃ w : Walk G mode k, w.start = u ∧ w.finish = v
def ReachesIn {n : ℕ} (G : Graph n) (mode : TraversalMode)
    (C : Finset (Fin n)) (u v : Fin n) : Prop :=
  ∃ k, ∃ w : Walk G mode k, w.IsPath ∧ w.StaysIn C ∧ w.start = u ∧ w.finish = v
def ReachesDuring {n : ℕ} (G : Graph n) (mode : TraversalMode)
    (a b : ℕ) (u v : Fin n) : Prop :=
  ∃ k, ∃ w : Walk G mode k, w.IsPath ∧ w.InWindow a b ∧ w.start = u ∧ w.finish = v







abbrev TemporalPath {n} (G : Graph n) (m : TraversalMode) (k : ℕ) := {w : Walk G m k // w.IsPath}
abbrev StrictPath {n} (G : Graph n) := TemporalPath G .strict
abbrev NonstrictPath {n} (G : Graph n) := TemporalPath G .nonstrict
abbrev StrictReachability {n} (G : Graph n) := Reaches G .strict
abbrev NonstrictReachability {n} (G : Graph n) := Reaches G .nonstrict

def graphReaches {n s} (G : InterpretedGraph n s) := Reaches G.graph s.mode



def bidirect {n} {s : Setting} (G : InterpretedGraph n s) :
    InterpretedGraph n { s with direction := .directed } where
  graph := G.graph
  admitted := ⟨trivial, G.admitted.2.1, fun h => ⟨trivial, (G.admitted.2.2 h).2⟩⟩




def Realizes {n k} (G : Graph n) (m : TraversalMode) (x : Fin (k+1) → Fin n) :=
  ∃ w : TemporalPath G m k, w.val.vertex = x

def SupportEquivalent {n} (G H : Graph n) (m l : TraversalMode) :=
  ∀ k (x : Fin (k+1) → Fin n), Realizes G m x ↔ Realizes H l x


end
end Lax330177.Paths

concepts.title: The temporal reachability graph
concepts.description:
Fix a traversal mode. The reachability graph is the static directed graph on the
original vertex set with an arc from u to v exactly when u and v are distinct
and a temporal path in that mode goes from u to v. Each arc records a whole
journey. Even undirected temporal graphs can have asymmetric reachability.
The zero-edge path witnesses reflexivity of the relation, while the graph omits
diagonal arcs.

[Strict and nonstrict reachability graphs on proper graphs.](Lax330177.ProperReachGraphs.html)

concepts.title: Three representations of temporal graphs
concepts.description:
A finite lifetime includes empty snapshots. Chronological lists enumerate distinct arc occurrences. Ties can be permuted. Undirected edges have both orientations.

- [Snapshots to labels and back.](Lax330177Proofs.Basic.snapshots_labels.html) Starting from snapshots, collecting the appearance times of each arc and reconstructing the snapshots recovers the original graph, including its lifetime.
- [Labels to snapshots and back.](Lax330177Proofs.Basic.labels_snapshots.html) Starting from a time-labelled footprint, taking its snapshots and collecting the labels again recovers the original footprint, label sets, and lifetime.
- [Events and adjacency.](Lax330177Proofs.Basic.stream_edges.html) At every time t, the snapshot reconstructed from the chronological event list contains the arc from u to v exactly when the original snapshot at t contains that arc.
- [Recovering an event list.](Lax330177Proofs.Basic.stream_roundtrip.html) Converting a chronological event list to snapshots and back preserves every event with its multiplicity. Only the order of events at the same time can change.
- [Snapshot adjacency and edge labels.](Lax330177.ActiveLabel.html) An arc is active at time t exactly when its label set contains t.

import Mathlib

/-!
---
title: Three representations of temporal graphs
type: definition
---
A finite lifetime includes empty snapshots. Chronological lists enumerate distinct arc occurrences. Ties can be permuted. Undirected edges have both orientations.

- [Snapshots to labels and back.](Lax330177Proofs.Basic.snapshots_labels.html) Starting from snapshots, collecting the appearance times of each arc and reconstructing the snapshots recovers the original graph, including its lifetime.
- [Labels to snapshots and back.](Lax330177Proofs.Basic.labels_snapshots.html) Starting from a time-labelled footprint, taking its snapshots and collecting the labels again recovers the original footprint, label sets, and lifetime.
- [Events and adjacency.](Lax330177Proofs.Basic.stream_edges.html) At every time t, the snapshot reconstructed from the chronological event list contains the arc from u to v exactly when the original snapshot at t contains that arc.
- [Recovering an event list.](Lax330177Proofs.Basic.stream_roundtrip.html) Converting a chronological event list to snapshots and back preserves every event with its multiplicity. Only the order of events at the same time can change.
- [Snapshot adjacency and edge labels.](Lax330177.ActiveLabel.html) An arc is active at time t exactly when its label set contains t.
-/
namespace Lax330177.Representations
noncomputable section
attribute [local instance] Classical.propDecidable
/-- A finite temporal graph with exactly `n` vertices. -/
structure Graph (n : ℕ) where
  lifetime : ℕ
  edge : Fin lifetime → Fin n → Fin n → Prop
  loopless : ∀ t u, ¬ edge t u u

/-- Symmetric snapshots represent undirected edges. -/
def IsUndirected {n : ℕ} (G : Graph n) : Prop :=
  ∀ t u v, G.edge t u v ↔ G.edge t v u


inductive Direction where
  | directed | undirected
  deriving DecidableEq

inductive TraversalMode where
  | strict | nonstrict
  deriving DecidableEq

def TimeLE (mode : TraversalMode) (a b : ℕ) : Prop :=
  match mode with
  | .strict => a < b
  | .nonstrict => a ≤ b

def ValidDirection {n : ℕ} (d : Direction) (G : Graph n) : Prop :=
  match d with
  | .directed => True
  | .undirected => IsUndirected G

def Footprint {n : ℕ} (G : Graph n) (u v : Fin n) : Prop := ∃ t, G.edge t u v

/-- Explicit footprint and finite labels, with no unused footprint edges. -/
structure LabeledGraph (n : ℕ) where
  lifetime : ℕ
  footprint : Fin n → Fin n → Prop
  labels : Fin n → Fin n → Finset (Fin lifetime)
  supported : ∀ u v, footprint u v ↔ (labels u v).Nonempty
  loopless : ∀ u, ¬ footprint u u

def toLabels {n : ℕ} (G : Graph n) : LabeledGraph n where
  lifetime := G.lifetime
  footprint := Footprint G
  labels u v := Finset.univ.filter (fun t => G.edge t u v)
  supported := by intro u v; simp [Footprint, Finset.Nonempty]
  loopless := by intro u ⟨t, h⟩; exact G.loopless t u h

def LabeledGraph.toSnapshots {n : ℕ} (G : LabeledGraph n) : Graph n where
  lifetime := G.lifetime
  edge t u v := t ∈ G.labels u v
  loopless := by
    intro t u h
    exact G.loopless u ((G.supported u u).mpr ⟨t, h⟩)




structure EventStream (n h : ℕ) where
  events : List (Fin h × Fin n × Fin n)
  chronological : events.Pairwise (fun a b => a.1 ≤ b.1)
  unique : events.Nodup
  loopless : ∀ e ∈ events, e.2.1 ≠ e.2.2

def EventStream.snapshots {n h} (s : EventStream n h) : Graph n where
  lifetime := h
  edge t u v := (t,u,v) ∈ s.events
  loopless := by intro t u he; exact s.loopless _ he rfl



def occurrences {n} (G : Graph n) :=
  Finset.univ.filter (fun e : Fin G.lifetime × Fin n × Fin n => G.edge e.1 e.2.1 e.2.2)

def streamOf {n} (G : Graph n) : EventStream n G.lifetime := by
  let xs := (occurrences G).toList
  let cmp (a b : Fin G.lifetime × Fin n × Fin n) := decide (a.1 ≤ b.1)
  refine ⟨xs.mergeSort cmp, ?_, ?_, ?_⟩
  · have h := List.pairwise_mergeSort (le := cmp)
        (by simpa [cmp] using (fun a b c => @le_trans _ _ a.1 b.1 c.1 : ∀ a b c : Fin G.lifetime × Fin n × Fin n, _))
        (by intro a b; simpa [cmp] using le_total a.1 b.1) xs
    simpa [cmp] using h
  · exact (List.mergeSort_perm xs cmp).nodup_iff.mpr (Finset.nodup_toList _)
  · rintro ⟨t,u,v⟩ he huv
    change u = v at huv
    subst v
    exact G.loopless t u (by simpa [xs, occurrences] using he)



end
end Lax330177.Representations

import Mathlib
import Lax330177.Representations

/-!
---
title: Temporal graph settings
type: definition
---
A setting selects direction, traversal mode and restrictions on the labelling. At a fixed time, two composable arcs u → v and v → w may coexist only when w = u. Opposite arcs may share a time, as may arcs with a common tail or a common head. For symmetric snapshots this is exactly the matching condition. Happy graphs are both simple and proper.
-/
namespace Lax330177.Settings
open Lax330177.Representations
noncomputable section
attribute [local instance] Classical.propDecidable
/-- Identity of the static edge, respecting the selected direction convention. -/
def SameStaticEdge (d : Direction) {n : ℕ} (u v x y : Fin n) : Prop :=
  match d with
  | .directed => u = x ∧ v = y
  | .undirected => (u = x ∧ v = y) ∨ (u = y ∧ v = x)
def IsSimple {n : ℕ} (G : Graph n) : Prop :=
  ∀ u v t s, G.edge t u v → G.edge s u v → t = s

def IsProper {n : ℕ} (d : Direction) (G : Graph n) : Prop :=
  ValidDirection d G ∧ ∀ t u v w, G.edge t u v → G.edge t v w → u = w

def IsHappy {n : ℕ} (d : Direction) (G : Graph n) : Prop :=
  IsSimple G ∧ IsProper d G

def LabelMultiplicityBound {n : ℕ} (G : Graph n) (b : ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∀ u v, ((toLabels G).labels u v).card ≤ b

structure Setting where
  direction : Direction
  mode : TraversalMode
  requireSimple : Bool := false
  requireProper : Bool := false

def Setting.Admits {n : ℕ} (s : Setting) (G : Graph n) : Prop :=
  ValidDirection s.direction G ∧ (s.requireSimple = true → IsSimple G) ∧
    (s.requireProper = true → IsProper s.direction G)

structure InterpretedGraph (n : ℕ) (s : Setting) where
  graph : Graph n
  admitted : s.Admits graph

abbrev StrictTemporalGraph (n : ℕ) (d : Direction) (simple proper : Bool) :=
  InterpretedGraph n ⟨d, .strict, simple, proper⟩
abbrev NonstrictTemporalGraph (n : ℕ) (d : Direction) (simple proper : Bool) :=
  InterpretedGraph n ⟨d, .nonstrict, simple, proper⟩

end
end Lax330177.Settings

concepts.title: Optimality under uniform traversal times
concepts.description:
With constant traversal time c, elapsed time equals total internal waiting plus
c times the number of hops. At c = 0, fastest and minimum-waiting paths coincide.
At c = 1 a hop contributes one unit even if the path never waits.

- [Elapsed time splits into travel and waiting.](Lax330177Proofs.UniformCosts.elapsed_eq.html) If every available traversal takes c time units, every feasible path has elapsed time equal to its total internal waiting time plus c times its number of hops.
- [Zero traversal time.](Lax330177Proofs.UniformCosts.zero_optima.html) With uniform traversal time zero, a feasible path is fastest exactly when it minimizes total internal waiting time.
- [Unit traversal time.](Lax330177Proofs.UniformCosts.unit_optima.html) With uniform traversal time one, a feasible path is fastest exactly when it minimizes the sum of its hop count and its total internal waiting time.

- [Unit traversal time.](Lax330177Proofs.UniformCosts.unit_optima.html) With uniform traversal time one, a feasible path is fastest exactly when it minimizes the sum of its hop count and its total internal waiting time.
-/

proofs.description: An undirected snapshot allows each active edge to be traversed in either direction. Replacing it by its two directed arcs permits exactly the same ordered steps at exactly the same times. The conditions on repeated vertices and on departure order are unchanged, so every timed path is preserved in both directions.

Use a graph on two vertices with one undirected edge. It is proper because there is no second edge incident to either endpoint. A walk can cross that edge and immediately cross it back at the same timestamp. Its two equal departure times satisfy the nonstrict rule and violate the strict rule.

On the undirected chain 0–1–2, edge 0–1 appears at time 1 and edge 1–2 at time 0. Each edge alone gives reachability between its endpoints in either mode. But the only path from 0 to 2 would have to use time 1 before time 0. Thus 0 reaches 1 and 1 reaches 2, while 0 cannot reach 2.

Give the undirected edge 1–2 time 0 and the edge 0–1 time 1. Each edge has one label and each snapshot contains just one edge, so the graph is happy. From 2 to 0 the chain uses times 0 then 1, valid in both modes. From 0 to 2 the only possible path requires those times in decreasing order.

An arc appears in the reconstructed snapshot at time t exactly when t belongs to its original label set. Collecting its appearance times therefore recovers that set. The footprint is recovered too, since its edges are precisely the pairs with nonempty label sets, and both conversions preserve the lifetime.

A strict path also satisfies the nonstrict timing rule. For the converse, take a nonstrict path. Consecutive edges form a two-step path with distinct outer vertices. Properness prevents both steps from using the same time. Their weakly increasing times must therefore increase strictly, giving a strict path with the same endpoints.

Consecutive steps have the form u → v → w with u and w distinct because the path never repeats a vertex. Properness forbids equal departure times for these two steps. Since the times are already weakly increasing, each is strictly smaller than its successor.

Let the single undirected edge between 0 and 1 appear at times 0 and 1. Each snapshot contains just that edge, so the graph is proper. Its two labels violate simplicity. In the directed interpretation, every two-step traversal returns to its starting vertex, so properness also holds there.

Let the only arcs be 0 → 1 and 1 → 2, both at time 0. Each has one label, so the graph is simple. They form a two-step path from 0 to 2 at the same time, so it fails properness. Taking both arcs at time 0 reaches vertex 2 nonstrictly from 0. A strict path would need two distinct times, since there is no direct arc.

Fix a time and an ordered pair of vertices. The label set of that pair contains the time exactly when the original snapshot contains the arc. Reconstructing the snapshot tests this same membership, so it recovers every arc at every time. The lifetime is copied as well, even when the final snapshot is empty.

List one event for every arc in every snapshot, then sort the list by time. Sorting preserves membership. Looking for the event with time t and endpoints u and v therefore succeeds exactly when the original snapshot at t contains the arc from u to v.

Forming snapshots from the stream records exactly which triples of time and endpoints occur. Converting back lists each recorded triple once. The original stream also lists each triple once, so the two lists are permutations of each other. Both are chronological, hence their orders can differ only among events at the same time.
Take a strict path between the two vertices and keep its vertices and departure times. Every strict increase is also a weak increase, so the same path witnesses nonstrict reachability.

Take the ordered vertex sequence of a path witnessing reachability in the first graph. Support equivalence supplies a path with that same sequence in the second graph, so its first and last vertices are the required endpoints. Exchanging the graphs proves the reverse implication.

Suppose one traversal departs at time a and a later traversal departs at b. With traversal time zero the first arrival is a, so feasibility requires a ≤ b. With traversal time one the arrival is a + 1. Since timestamps are integers, a + 1 ≤ b holds exactly when a < b. Applying this to every pair of steps gives both equivalences.

Fix the vertex sequence and its departure times. Both path definitions require distinct vertices and an available edge at every departure. For uniform time zero, arrival before or at the next departure means that departure times are weakly increasing. For uniform time one, it means that the integer times are strictly increasing. Thus the same sequences satisfy either description exactly in the stated mode.

Choose a path witnessing reachability. With uniform traversal time one, feasibility requires strictly increasing integer departures. With time zero, it requires weakly increasing departures. In either case the same timed path witnesses reachability in the corresponding mode. Reading the timing equivalence in reverse gives the converse.

If a walk visits a vertex twice, delete the steps between those visits. The remaining prefix and suffix join at the same vertex. Their departure times form a subsequence of the original times, so they still satisfy the chosen timing rule. Each deletion shortens the walk and preserves its endpoints. Eventually no vertex repeats, giving a path. Conversely, every path is already a walk.

Vertices 0 and 2 are distinct, so every path needs at least one traversal and takes at least c time units. A direct traversal attains both bounds and has zero waiting, whether it departs at 0 or at 3. Departing at 0 gives arrival c, the earliest possible from release time 0. Departing at 3 uses the last available snapshot. Comparing the two direct paths shows that the early one loses on latest departure and the late one loses on foremost arrival.

Depart on the two arcs at times 0 and c. The second departure is exactly the first arrival, so total waiting is zero, the least possible. The direct arc uses one hop instead of two. With c equal to zero the detour also takes zero elapsed time and is fastest. With c equal to one it takes two units, while the direct arc takes only one.

Without the shortcut, every path from 0 to 2 must traverse both arcs of the chain. Departing at times 0 and 3 therefore gives a shortest path, but it waits at vertex 1 from time c until time 3. Departing instead at 0 and c removes that positive wait while keeping both traversals. This second path both waits less and finishes sooner, for c equal to zero or one.
The label set collects exactly the appearance times of the ordered pair.
Forget the restriction in one direction. Conversely, every vertex on the witnessing path belongs to the full set.
Keep the path and use containment for each visited vertex.
Repeating a static edge forces an endpoint to occur at two different positions.

Both graphs omit diagonal arcs. For distinct vertices, their adjacency agrees
because strict and nonstrict paths give the same reachability on a proper graph.
The zero-edge path at the vertex has no timing constraints.
Different traversals have different times.
Both conditions exclude exactly the same simultaneous two-step traversals with distinct outer vertices. Symmetry supplies the undirected graph condition.
A repeated edge-time occurrence would use the same static edge twice.
The two occurrences have different times but use the same undirected edge.

For each of hop count, elapsed time, arrival time and total waiting, collect the values attained by feasible paths. If a feasible path exists, each collection is a nonempty set of natural numbers and has a least member. A path attaining that member is optimal for the chosen criterion. For latest departure, minimize the deadline minus the departure time. Every feasible departure is at or before the deadline, so a path minimizing this difference departs as late as possible.

Split the interval from first departure to final arrival into the traversals and the gaps between them. Each traversal contributes c time units. Each gap runs from one arrival to the next departure and contributes exactly the waiting time there. These pieces cover the interval in order, so elapsed time equals total waiting plus c times the hop count. A zero-hop path departs and arrives at the same instant, making both sides zero.

Set c to one in the elapsed-time identity. A path with k hops and w units of waiting takes k + w units from departure to arrival. Comparing this sum over all feasible paths is therefore exactly the comparison that defines a fastest path.

Set c to zero in the elapsed-time identity. Every path then has elapsed time equal to its own waiting time. Consequently two feasible paths compare in exactly the same order under the two criteria, including ties, and their sets of minimizers coincide.
